title: Bangkok in 4 days: temples, street food and hidden corners
description: A four-day Bangkok itinerary pairing the great temples of Rattanakosin with Chinatown street food, a Green Lung bike ride and a few local favourites. Suits first-time visitors who love eating well and exploring by boat, skytrain and on foot.

data.name: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew
data.description: Bangkok's royal showpiece: gilded halls and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha. Cover shoulders and knees, and arrive early before the courtyards fill.
data.address: Na Phra Lan Rd, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200

data.name: Lunch at Supanniga Eating Room (Tha Tien)
data.description: Family-style Thai cooking with regional influences, a short walk from Wat Pho and Tha Tien pier. Order several dishes to share.
data.address: 392/25-26 Maha Rat Rd, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200

data.name: Wat Pho
data.description: See the enormous Reclining Buddha and the temple's cloisters of stupas. Wat Pho is also the home of traditional Thai massage.
data.address: 2 Sanam Chai Rd, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200

data.name: Wat Arun
data.description: Hop on the short cross-river ferry from Tha Tien to the Temple of Dawn, and climb its steep porcelain-studded prang for views back over the river.
data.address: 158 Thanon Wang Doem, Wat Arun, Bangkok Yai, Bangkok 10600

data.name: Wat Traimit (Golden Buddha)
data.description: A start to Chinatown with the solid-gold Buddha statue, one of Bangkok's most extraordinary sights, on the edge of Yaowarat.
data.address: 661 Charoen Krung Rd, Talat Noi, Samphanthawong, Bangkok 10100

data.name: Lunch at Nai Mong Hoi Thod
data.description: A long-running Yaowarat stall known for crispy oyster omelettes. Check opening days before you go, as hours vary.
data.address: 539 Phlap Phla Chai Rd, Pom Prap, Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok 10100

data.name: Talat Noi walk
data.description: Wander the riverside lanes of Talat Noi: old shophouses, Chinese shrines, street art, scrap-metal workshops and small coffee shops.
data.address: Soi Wanit 2, Talat Noi, Samphanthawong, Bangkok 10100

data.name: Seafood dinner at T&K Seafood
data.description: Chinatown at night: pavement tables on Yaowarat serving grilled prawns, tom yum goong and steamed fish with lime and chilli.

data.name: Jim Thompson House
data.description: A compound of traditional teak houses once lived in by the American silk entrepreneur, filled with Asian art and set in a leafy garden.
data.address: 6 Soi Kasem San 2, Rama I Rd, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330

data.name: Lunch at Somtum Der
data.description: North-eastern Thai cooking on Sala Daeng Road: papaya salads in several styles, grilled chicken and sticky rice.
data.address: 5/5 Sala Daeng Rd, Silom, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500

data.name: Lumphini Park
data.description: Bangkok's central green space, with a lake, shaded paths and the odd monitor lizard. A good place to slow down in the afternoon heat.
data.address: Rama IV Rd, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330

data.name: Tom yum noodles at Jeh O Chula
data.description: A cult-favourite late-opening spot near Chulalongkorn University, famous for tom yum Mama noodles loaded with seafood. Expect a queue.
data.address: 113 Soi Charat Mueang, Banthat Thong Rd, Rong Mueang, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330

data.name: Cycle Bang Krachao, the Green Lung
data.description: Take the ferry across the Chao Phraya to this leafy river bend and cycle flat paved paths through gardens, mangrove and fruit orchards.
data.address: Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park and Botanical Garden, Bang Kachao, Phra Pradaeng, Samut Prakan 10130

data.name: Lunch at Polo Fried Chicken (Soi Polo)
data.description: A no-frills institution for garlicky north-eastern fried chicken, served with papaya salad and sticky rice.
data.address: 137/1-3 Soi Sanam Khli (Soi Polo), Wireless Rd, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330

data.name: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre
data.description: A contemporary art centre next to Siam, with changing exhibitions across several floors and a good place to browse for local design.
data.address: 939 Rama I Rd, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330

data.name: Sunset drinks at Sky Bar, lebua at State Tower
data.description: Finish with cocktails high above the Chao Phraya, with the city lights coming on. A smart-casual dress code applies.
data.address: 1055 Si Lom Rd, Silom, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500

data.name: Sala Rattanakosin Bangkok
data.description: Small boutique hotel on the Chao Phraya beside Tha Tien pier, a short walk from Wat Pho and the Grand Palace, with river views toward Wat Arun.
data.address: 39 Maha Rat Rd, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200

data.name: Siam@Siam Design Hotel Bangkok
data.description: Design-led hotel on Rama I Road, close to National Stadium BTS station, Jim Thompson House and the Siam shopping area, with easy skytrain access.
data.address: 865 Rama I Rd, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330

data.name: Raan Jay Fai
data.address: 327 Maha Chai Rd, Samran Rat, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200
data.description: Michelin-starred street-food kitchen of the goggle-wearing Jay Fai, famed for crab omelette and drunken noodles. Book ahead.

data.name: Thipsamai Pad Thai
data.address: 313-315 Maha Chai Rd, Samran Rat, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200
data.description: A Bangkok pad thai institution near Pratu Phi, known for noodles wrapped in a thin egg net and fresh orange juice.

data.name: Krua Apsorn (Dinso Road)
data.address: 169 Dinso Rd, Sao Chingcha, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200
data.description: Beloved for royal-style home cooking, especially its crab omelette and stir-fried crab with yellow curry. Closed Sundays.

data.name: Err Urban Rustic Thai
data.address: 56/10 Soi Sukhumvit 55 (Thong Lo), Khlong Tan Nuea, Watthana, Bangkok 10110
data.description: Casual Thai sharing plates inspired by old Bangkok street food, from the team behind Bo.lan. Open evenings.

data.name: Baan Silapin (Artist's House)
data.address: 315 Soi Phet Kasem 28, Khlong Bang Luang, Phasi Charoen, Bangkok 10160
data.description: A century-old wooden house over a canal on the Thonburi side, now an arts space with workshops, a gallery and a cafe. Check ahead for puppet shows.

data.name: Santa Cruz Church and Kudeejeen
data.address: Soi Kudi Chin, Wat Kanlaya, Thon Buri, Bangkok 10600
data.description: A pastel Renaissance-style church in the old Portuguese quarter of Thonburi, with small lanes and a local sweet, khanom farang, to try nearby.

data.name: Pak Khlong Talat flower market
data.address: Chak Phet Rd, Wang Burapha Phirom, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200
data.description: Bangkok's wholesale flower market near Memorial Bridge, a riot of marigolds and orchids and best seen early in the morning.

data.name: Loha Prasat (Metal Castle)
data.address: Wat Ratchanatdaram, Maha Chai Rd, Bowon Niwet, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok 10200
data.description: A rare multi-spired metal temple at Wat Ratchanatdaram, with a quiet interior staircase and views from the top.

data.name: Universal power adapter (Thailand uses types A, B, C and F)
Modest outfit for temples (covered shoulders and knees)
Comfortable slip-on walking sandals or shoes

title: Tokyo in 7 days: temples, ramen and neighbourhood life
description: A week in Tokyo that blends the big sights with the city's best eating and a day trip to Kamakura. Suits first-time visitors who enjoy walking, queueing for a good bowl of noodles and finding quieter corners between the crowds.

data.name: Senso-ji and Nakamise-dori
data.description: Tokyo's oldest temple, reached through the Kaminarimon gate and the souvenir stalls of Nakamise-dori. Arrive early for a calmer courtyard.

data.name: Tendon lunch at Daikokuya Tempura
data.description: A historic tempura house near Senso-ji, first opened in the 19th century, serving tendon: tempura on rice with a sweet-savoury sauce.

data.name: Tokyo National Museum and Ueno Park
data.description: Japan's largest collection of art and archaeology, set in leafy Ueno Park. Check the museum's closing day before you go.

data.name: Tonkatsu dinner at Ponta Honke
data.description: A Ueno yoshoku restaurant dating back to the early 1900s, known as a birthplace of tonkatsu, the breaded pork cutlet.

data.name: Meiji Jingu
data.description: Walk through a forested torii-lined approach to Tokyo's grand Shinto shrine, an oasis of calm in the middle of Harajuku.

data.name: Lunch at Tonkatsu Maisen Aoyama Honten
data.description: A famous tonkatsu restaurant in a converted bathhouse, a short stroll from Omotesando. Order the thick-cut pork loin set.

data.name: Shibuya Sky
data.description: An open-air rooftop observatory above Shibuya Scramble Square, with sweeping views over Shibuya Crossing and out to Tokyo Tower.

data.name: Sushi dinner at Uobei Shibuya Dogenzaka
data.description: A fast and fun conveyor-style sushi restaurant where you order by touch screen and the plates arrive by little express trains.

data.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
data.description: A spacious garden blending Japanese, French and English landscapes, with a glasshouse and plenty of quiet lawns.

data.name: Tsukemen at Fuunji
data.description: A counter-only Shinjuku-edge favourite for tsukemen: thick noodles dipped in a rich fish and pork broth. Expect a short queue.

data.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory
data.description: City views from the twin towers of Tokyo's city hall, with Mount Fuji visible on clear days.

data.name: Yakitori dinner in Omoide Yokocho
data.description: A narrow lane of smoky grill stalls beside the Shinjuku rail tracks. Pick a seat at a counter and order skewers and a drink.

data.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
data.description: Graze through the market's lanes for tamagoyaki, grilled seafood, pickles and sweet treats. Many stalls wind down by early afternoon.

data.name: Sushi lunch at Sushizanmai Honten
data.description: The flagship of a well-known sushi chain with counter seating and a wide choice of nigiri. A simple, reliable way to try Tsukiji-style fish.

data.name: Hamarikyu Gardens
data.description: A tidal-pond garden from the Edo era, with skyscrapers rising behind the pines and a teahouse on the water.

data.name: Tsukemen at Rokurinsha, Tokyo Ramen Street
data.description: A well-known tsukemen shop in the ramen arcade beneath Tokyo Station. Queues are normal, but they move steadily.
data.address: B1F First Avenue Tokyo Station, 1-9-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda City, Tokyo 100-0005

data.name: teamLab Planets
data.description: A walk-through digital art museum where you wade barefoot through water and mirrored rooms. Book a time slot ahead of your visit.

data.name: Lunch at Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai
data.description: An Edo-themed food and bathhouse complex beside Toyosu Market, with several seafood counters and restaurants to choose from.

data.name: Kiyosumi Gardens
data.description: A Meiji-era stroll garden with stepping stones across a central pond, set in a pleasant neighbourhood of small cafes.

data.name: Dinner at Komagata Dojo
data.description: An Edo-period restaurant in Asakusa famous for dojo (loach), served in a shallow iron pot. Adventurous, and a real taste of old Tokyo.

data.name: Kotoku-in (Great Buddha of Kamakura)
data.description: A monumental bronze Buddha that has sat in the open air for centuries. Allow time to walk around the back as well.

data.name: Shirasu lunch at Hase Shokudo
data.description: A casual spot near Hase Station serving local whitebait (shirasu) rice bowls, tempura and other Shonan seafood.

data.name: Hase-dera Temple
data.description: A hillside temple of hydrangeas, a golden Kannon statue and sea views, with a small cave shrine at the base.

data.name: Tsurugaoka Hachimangu
data.description: Kamakura's main shrine, reached by a long cherry-lined approach from the sea. Climb the steps for a view back down the avenue.

data.name: Yanaka Ginza and Yanaka Cemetery
data.description: A retro shopping street in one of the few old districts that survived the war, with croquette stalls, cat motifs and quiet temple lanes.

data.name: Nezu Shrine
data.description: An atmospheric shrine with a tunnel of vermilion torii gates and a pretty garden, set in a quiet Bunkyo neighbourhood.

data.name: Lunch at Kayaba Coffee
data.description: A classic kissaten in a renovated wooden building, best known for its egg sandwich and coffee. Check its closing day before you go.

data.name: Shimokitazawa
data.description: Browse vintage shops, record stores and small cafes in Tokyo's creative neighbourhood, then head back at your own pace.

data.name: Hotel Gracery Shinjuku
data.description: A well-placed Shinjuku hotel in Kabukicho, a short walk from Shinjuku Station and the Yamanote line, with a Godzilla head on the roof.

data.name: Tsunahachi Shinjuku Honten
data.description: A historic Shinjuku tempura house dating back to the 1920s, serving counter and table tempura sets near Shinjuku-sanchome.

data.name: Nodaiwa Azabu Iikura Honten
data.description: A centuries-old unagi specialist near Azabu-juban, serving grilled eel over rice. A refined, traditional meal.

data.name: Sosakumenkobo Nakiryu
data.description: A sought-after tantanmen shop in Otsuka, known for its layered broth and house-made noodles. Expect a queue.

data.name: Gyukatsu Motomura Shibuya
data.address: B1F Ohno Building No.2, 3-18-10 Shibuya, Shibuya City, Tokyo 150-0002
data.description: A popular beef cutlet restaurant where you cook thin slices on a hot stone at the table. Queues build at peak times.

data.name: Gotokuji Temple
data.description: A quiet Setagaya temple known as a birthplace of the maneki-neko, with hundreds of small white lucky cats left by visitors.

data.name: Nezu Museum
data.description: A serene collection of Japanese and East Asian art, backed by a lovely garden with tea houses, minutes from Omotesando.

data.name: Rikugien Garden
data.description: An Edo-era strolling garden in Bunkyo with a large pond and winding paths, far less crowded than the better-known gardens.

data.name: Todoroki Valley Park
data.description: A wooded ravine tucked into Setagaya, with a stream-side path, a small shrine and a cool, green hush in the middle of the city.

data.name: Plug adapter for Japan (type A and B, 100 V)
Layers and a light rain jacket
Small coin purse and some cash
Hand towel (public restrooms often lack dryers)

title: Seoul in 5 days: palaces, markets and neighbourhood food
description: A five-day Seoul itinerary that mixes royal palaces and hanok lanes with market food, hearty noodle and barbecue meals, and a few of the city's creative neighbourhoods. Suits first-time visitors who enjoy walking, eating and a bit of museum time.

data.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
data.description: Seoul's grandest Joseon-era palace, with ceremonial gates, a lakeside pavilion and a changing of the guard outside the main gate. Wear comfortable shoes.

data.name: Lunch at Tosokchon Samgyetang
data.description: A hanok-style institution near the palace, serving samgyetang: a whole young chicken stuffed with rice and ginseng in a bubbling broth.

data.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
data.description: Wander the hillside lanes of traditional hanok houses, with city views and small galleries. It is a residential area, so keep your voice down.

data.name: Dinner at Gwangjang Market
data.description: One of Seoul's oldest markets, with food stalls serving bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap and other classics at shared tables.

data.name: Changdeokgung Palace
data.description: A UNESCO World Heritage palace that blends into its hillside, known for its rear garden. Some areas are visited on timed guided tours, so check ahead.

data.name: Lunch at Myeongdong Kyoja
data.description: A long-running Myeongdong favourite for kalguksu, hand-cut noodles in a peppery chicken broth, served with dumplings and garlicky kimchi.

data.name: N Seoul Tower and Namsan Park
data.description: Walk up through Namsan's wooded paths to the tower for views over the whole city. Time your visit for late afternoon light.

data.name: Naengmyeon dinner at Woo Lae Oak
data.description: A veteran Pyongyang-style naengmyeon restaurant in Euljiro, serving buckwheat noodles in a cold, clear beef broth. Share a plate of bulgogi alongside.

data.name: National Museum of Korea
data.description: One of the largest museums in Asia, with a deep collection of Korean art and archaeology, from ancient ceramics to Buddhist sculpture.

data.name: Galbi lunch at Maple Tree House (Itaewon)
data.description: A popular Korean barbecue restaurant in Itaewon, known for marinated galbi grilled at the table.

data.name: Leeum Museum of Art
data.description: A striking private museum in Hannam-dong pairing traditional Korean art with contemporary works, in buildings by renowned architects.

data.name: Naksan Park and the Seoul City Wall
data.description: A short climb along a stretch of the old city wall, with fine views of the city and the hilltop mural lanes of Ihwa.

data.name: Seolleongtang at Imun Seolnongtang
data.description: A famously old Jongno restaurant, founded in the early 1900s, serving seolleongtang: a milky beef-bone soup you season at the table.

data.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza
data.description: Zaha Hadid's curving silver landmark, with exhibitions, design shops and a landscaped roof. The area around it is also good for fabric and fashion browsing.

data.name: Dakhanmari at Jinokhwa Halmae
data.description: The original dakhanmari alley's best-known spot, serving a whole chicken simmered with potatoes and rice cakes, finished with hand-cut noodles.

data.name: Seoul Forest
data.description: A large park of meadows, ponds and tree-lined paths, popular with locals for picnics and cycling. A relaxed way to start the last day.

data.name: Brunch at Daelim Changgo, Seongsu
data.description: A warehouse cafe and gallery that helped kick-start Seongsu's cafe scene, with high ceilings and a relaxed, creative crowd.

data.name: Bongeunsa Temple
data.description: A working Buddhist temple tucked between Gangnam's towers, with a large Buddha statue and a peaceful courtyard.

data.name: Starfield Library
data.description: A two-storey open library inside COEX Mall, with towering shelves that make it one of Seoul's most photographed interiors.

data.name: L7 Myeongdong by LOTTE
data.description: A comfortable, well-located hotel close to Myeongdong station, with easy subway links and a short walk from several of the restaurants and sights in this itinerary.

data.name: Hadongkwan
data.description: A venerable Myeongdong restaurant known for gomtang, a clear beef soup served with rice. A simple, comforting breakfast or lunch.

data.name: Geumdwaeji Sikdang
data.description: A Sindang pork barbecue spot known for grilling on cast iron over coal briquettes. No reservations, so expect a queue.

data.name: Pyeongyang Myeonok (Jangchung-dong)
data.description: A long-standing Pyongyang-style naengmyeon restaurant in Jangchung-dong, a good alternative to Woo Lae Oak. Closed on Mondays.

data.name: Sanchon
data.description: A Buddhist temple-food restaurant in Insadong, serving seasonal vegetarian dishes in a traditional setting.

data.name: Tongin Market (Seochon)
data.description: A small neighbourhood market where you swap coins for dishes at the dosirak cafe and build your own lunchbox.

data.name: Seonyudo Park
data.description: A park built on a former water-treatment plant on an island in the Han River, with gardens, walkways and skyline views.

data.name: Gilsangsa Temple
data.description: A tranquil temple in leafy Seongbuk-dong, a quiet escape that is a world away from central Seoul.

data.name: Ikseon-dong Hanok Street
data.description: A tiny maze of renovated hanok alleys filled with cafes and small restaurants, close to Jongno 3-ga station.

data.name: Plug adapter for Korea (type C or F, 220 V)
Comfortable, grippy walking shoes (hilly lanes and stairs)
Some cash for markets and small stalls
Passport and entry authorisation (check K-ETA for your nationality)

title: Hanoi in 4 days: street food, temples and lakeside walks
description: Four days in Vietnam's capital, mixing street-food classics like pho, bun cha and cha ca with temples, museums and slow mornings by Hoan Kiem Lake. Suits first-time visitors who want to eat well without rushing.

data.name: Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son Temple
data.description: Stroll the lakeside path and cross the red Huc Bridge to Ngoc Son Temple on its small island. A calm introduction to the city before the Old Quarter gets busy.
data.address: Dinh Tien Hoang Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: Pho Gia Truyen
data.description: A long-established Old Quarter pho shop on Bat Dan Street, known for clear beef broth and a very short menu. Expect to share a table and eat quickly.
data.address: 49 Bat Dan Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: Dong Xuan Market and the Old Quarter streets
data.description: Wander Hanoi's best-known covered market and the surrounding 36 Streets, where many lanes still specialise in one trade. Good for snacks, textiles and souvenirs.
data.address: Dong Xuan Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: Cha Ca Thang Long
data.description: Turmeric-marinated fish sizzled at your table with dill and spring onion, served with rice noodles and herbs. A family-run restaurant that serves almost nothing else.
data.address: 6B Duong Thanh Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex and One Pillar Pagoda
data.description: See Ba Dinh Square, the stilt house in the gardens and the One Pillar Pagoda. The mausoleum interior has limited visiting days and an annual maintenance closure, so check first and dress modestly.
data.address: Hung Vuong Street, Ba Dinh, Hanoi

data.name: Tuyet Bun Cha 34
data.description: Charcoal-grilled pork patties and pork belly in a sweet-sharp broth with rice vermicelli and herbs, the classic northern lunch. A no-frills street-food spot.
data.address: 34 Hang Than Street, Ba Dinh, Hanoi

data.name: Temple of Literature
data.description: Founded in the 11th century as a Confucian temple and later Vietnam's first national university. Walk the courtyards, ponds and stone stelae set on tortoises.
data.address: 58 Quoc Tu Giam Street, Dong Da, Hanoi

data.name: Tran Quoc Pagoda and West Lake
data.description: One of Hanoi's oldest Buddhist pagodas, on a small peninsula in West Lake. A peaceful place to watch the light fade over the water.
data.address: Thanh Nien Road, Tay Ho, Hanoi

data.name: Hoa Lo Prison Memorial
data.description: A former French colonial prison turned museum, telling the story of Vietnamese revolutionaries held here and, later, of US pilots detained during the war.
data.address: 1 Hoa Lo Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: Quan An Ngon
data.description: Dishes from across Vietnam cooked at open street-food stations in a colonial villa courtyard. An easy way to try banh xeo, bun cha and more in one sitting.
data.address: 18 Phan Boi Chau Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: Vietnamese Women's Museum
data.description: A thoughtful museum on women's roles in family life, war and everyday work, with ethnic-minority textiles and a good gift shop. A cool break from the street.
data.address: 36 Ly Thuong Kiet Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre
data.description: Water puppetry with live folk music, an art form from the northern rice-paddy villages. Book ahead and check the day's performance times.
data.address: 57B Dinh Tien Hoang Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: Vietnam Museum of Ethnology
data.description: A well-regarded museum on Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups, with an outdoor garden of traditional stilt houses and communal houses. Take a taxi or ride-hail from the centre.
data.address: Nguyen Van Huyen Road, Cau Giay, Hanoi

data.name: Bun Cha Huong Lien
data.description: The bun cha restaurant made famous by a 2016 meal with a visiting US president. Charcoal-grilled pork with noodles and herbs; order a side of nem cua be.
data.address: 24 Le Van Huu Street, Hai Ba Trung, Hanoi

data.name: Cafe Giang egg coffee
data.description: Taste egg coffee, the whipped egg-yolk and coffee drink created in Hanoi in the 1940s. This small cafe is its best-known home.
data.address: 39 Nguyen Huu Huan Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: St Joseph's Cathedral and the lanes around it
data.description: A neo-Gothic cathedral from the 1880s and the cafe-lined lanes behind it, a gentle last wander before heading to the airport or your next stop.
data.address: 40 Nha Chung Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: La Siesta Classic Ma May
data.description: Well-reviewed Old Quarter hotel on Ma May Street, a short walk from Hoan Kiem Lake and the night market, with attentive service and a good breakfast. Convenient for the first day and most of the trip.
data.address: 94 Ma May Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

data.name: Bun Cha Ta
data.address: 21 Nguyen Huu Huan Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi
data.description: Homestyle bun cha across several floors in the Old Quarter, with smoky grilled pork, herbs and a sweet-tangy dipping sauce.

data.name: Mien Luon Dong Thinh
data.address: 87 Hang Dieu Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi
data.description: Decades-old eel specialist. Order the dry noodle dish with crisp eel, herbs, peanuts and fried shallots.

data.name: Sente
data.address: 20 Nguyen Quang Bich Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi
data.description: Calm, green restaurant built around lotus, using flowers, seeds and roots in modern Vietnamese dishes.

data.name: Chapter
data.address: 12C Chan Cam Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi
data.description: An intimate restaurant with an open charcoal grill, serving a seasonal tasting menu rooted in northern Vietnamese cooking. Book ahead.

data.name: Banh Mi 25
data.address: 25 Hang Ca Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi
data.description: Hanoi's take on banh mi in a crisp baguette, sold from a busy Hang Ca shopfront. A quick, cheap lunch between sights.

data.name: Bach Ma Temple
data.address: 76 Hang Buom Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi
data.description: One of the oldest temples in Hanoi, tucked into the Old Quarter on Hang Buom Street and often overlooked.

data.name: Long Bien Bridge
data.description: A rusty French-era steel bridge over the Red River. Walk or cycle part of it early or late for views of the city and the river's sandbanks.

data.name: Quan Thanh Temple
data.address: 194 Quan Thanh Street, Ba Dinh, Hanoi
data.description: A quiet Taoist temple near West Lake with a large bronze statue of Tran Vu, the guardian of the north. Much less visited than the big sights.

data.name: Cafe Pho Co
data.address: 11 Hang Gai Street, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi
data.description: A cafe reached through a silk shop on Hang Gai Street, with a hidden courtyard and a lake-view upper floor.

data.name: Modest tops and trousers or skirt for temples
Passport and any entry visa confirmation

title: Bali in 1 week: temples, rice terraces and beaches
description: A week in Bali split between Ubud's temples, rice terraces and cooking classes and the coast around Seminyak, Uluwatu and Canggu. Suits first-time visitors who want culture, good food and some beach time.

data.name: Ubud Palace and Ubud Art Market
data.description: Step into the courtyards of Puri Saren Agung, Ubud's royal palace, then browse the art market across the road for crafts, textiles and carvings.
data.address: Jl. Raya Ubud No.8, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka
data.description: A famous Ubud warung for babi guling, Bali's celebratory roast suckling pig, served with rice, crackling and spicy lawar.
data.address: Jl. Tegal Sari No.2, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Museum Puri Lukisan
data.description: One of Bali's oldest art museums, set in tropical gardens, with Balinese painting and carving that traces how Ubud became an art centre.
data.address: Jl. Raya Ubud, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Legong dance at Ubud Palace
data.description: An evening of Balinese dance and gamelan music in the palace courtyard. Check the programme and buy tickets at the venue.
data.address: Jl. Raya Ubud No.8, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Tirta Empul Temple
data.description: A holy spring temple in Tampaksiring where Balinese Hindus take part in ritual purification in the pools. Wear a sarong, and be respectful if you are watching.
data.address: Jl. Tirta, Manukaya, Tampaksiring, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Tegallalang Rice Terrace
data.description: Stepped rice terraces north of Ubud, irrigated by the traditional subak system. Walk the paths for the best views.
data.address: Jl. Raya Tegallalang, Tegallalang, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Warung Makan Teges
data.description: A family warung known for nasi campur: a plate of rice with small portions of pork, chicken or vegetables and sambal. Informal, local and good value.
data.address: Jl. Cok Rai Pudak, Peliatan, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk
data.description: A gentle ridge-top path between two rivers with views over green valleys, best in the golden light of late afternoon.
data.address: Campuhan Ridge Walk, Jl. Raya Campuhan, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Paon Bali Cooking Class
data.description: A hands-on Balinese cooking class in the village of Laplapan, typically starting with a market visit and ending with a meal of what you have cooked.
data.address: Jl. Raya Laplapan, Petulu, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary
data.description: A forest reserve with three Hindu temples and troops of long-tailed macaques. Keep food and loose items out of sight.
data.address: Jl. Monkey Forest, Padangtegal, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Yoga class at The Yoga Barn
data.description: An open-air yoga and wellness centre in Ubud with daily classes for different levels. Check the timetable and book a class.
data.address: Jl. Hanoman, Padangtegal, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Hujan Locale
data.description: Regional Indonesian dishes reinterpreted with local ingredients, a good way to sample flavours from across the archipelago in one meal.
data.address: Jl. Sri Wedari No.5, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave)
data.description: An 11th-century cave sanctuary with a carved demon-mouth entrance, bathing pools and a garden of shrines. A sarong is required.
data.address: Jl. Raya Goa Gajah, Bedulu, Blahbatuh, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
data.description: A broad, easy-to-reach waterfall south of Ubud with a viewing platform and a pool at its base. Wear sandals with grip for the steps.
data.address: Jl. Tegenungan, Kemenuh, Sukawati, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Bebek Bengil (Dirty Duck Diner)
data.description: A garden restaurant on Jalan Hanoman famed for its crispy duck. A relaxed lunch before a spa session.
data.address: Jl. Hanoman, Padangtegal, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Karsa Spa
data.description: Traditional Balinese massage and spa treatments in a quiet garden setting on the northern edge of Ubud.
data.address: Jl. Bangkiang Sidem, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Merah Putih
data.description: Modern Indonesian cooking in a striking, soaring open dining room in Petitenget. An easy first meal in Seminyak after the transfer from Ubud.
data.address: Jl. Petitenget No.100X, Kerobokan Kelod, Kuta Utara, Badung, Bali

data.name: Jalan Kayu Aya boutiques
data.description: Browse the boutiques, ceramics, linen and swimwear shops and cafes along Seminyak's Jalan Kayu Aya.
data.address: Jl. Kayu Aya, Seminyak, Kuta, Badung, Bali

data.name: Pura Petitenget
data.description: A beachside sea temple in Seminyak, important in the local ritual calendar. Dress respectfully and view from outside unless ceremonies are open to visitors.
data.address: Jl. Petitenget, Kerobokan Kelod, Kuta Utara, Badung, Bali

data.name: Sunset at Potato Head Beach Club
data.description: A beachfront club with ocean-facing lawns and a relaxed atmosphere. Come for sunset drinks and dinner.
data.address: Jl. Petitenget No.51B, Kerobokan Kelod, Kuta Utara, Badung, Bali

data.name: Padang Padang Beach
data.description: A small cove reached through a narrow gap in the cliffs, popular with surfers and swimmers. Visit at a suitable tide.
data.address: Jl. Labuan Sait, Pecatu, Kuta Selatan, Badung, Bali

data.name: Single Fin
data.description: A clifftop surf bar above Suluban beach with sweeping ocean views, casual food and cold drinks.
data.address: Jl. Pantai Suluban, Pecatu, Kuta Selatan, Badung, Bali

data.name: Pura Luhur Uluwatu
data.description: An 11th-century sea temple on a high cliff above the Indian Ocean. Watch your belongings around the resident macaques.
data.address: Pura Luhur Uluwatu, Pecatu, Kuta Selatan, Badung, Bali

data.name: Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu
data.description: A chanting chorus performs the Kecak dance at sunset in the cliff-top amphitheatre beside the temple.
data.address: Pura Luhur Uluwatu, Pecatu, Kuta Selatan, Badung, Bali

data.name: Beginner surf lesson at Batu Bolong Beach
data.description: A beginner-friendly surf break in Canggu. Book a lesson with a licensed local surf school that provides boards and instruction.
data.address: Batu Bolong Beach, Jl. Pantai Batu Bolong, Canggu, Badung, Bali

data.name: The Shady Shack
data.description: A long-running plant-based cafe in Canggu with a colourful dining room and a relaxed beach-town atmosphere.
data.address: Jl. Tanah Barak No.53, Canggu, Kuta Utara, Badung, Bali

data.name: Tanah Lot
data.description: A sea temple on a rocky outcrop on the Tabanan coast, atmospheric at sunset. It is busy, so arrive early and allow time for the drive.
data.address: Jl. Raya Tanah Lot, Beraban, Kediri, Tabanan, Bali

data.name: Komaneka at Monkey Forest
data.description: Well-reviewed boutique resort on Jalan Monkey Forest, a short walk from the Monkey Forest and Ubud Palace. A convenient base for the first four nights in Ubud, with a pool, spa and restaurant.
data.address: Jl. Monkey Forest, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali

data.name: Alila Seminyak
data.description: A resort with pools and sleek modern design on Jalan Taman Ganesha, a few minutes from Seminyak Beach. Base yourself here for the last three nights, with Canggu and Uluwatu both a drive away.
data.address: Jl. Taman Ganesha No.9, Petitenget, Seminyak, Badung, Bali

data.name: Warung Biah Biah
data.description: A casual Ubud warung on Jalan Goutama serving Balinese small plates to share, popular with locals and visitors alike.

data.name: Naughty Nuri's Warung
data.address: Jl. Raya Sanggingan 88X, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali
data.description: An Ubud institution for sticky grilled pork ribs and martinis. Casual, loud and sociable.

data.name: Warung Mendez
data.address: Jl. Raya Penestanan, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali
data.description: A well-regarded local restaurant in Penestanan serving Balinese and Indonesian home cooking at friendly prices.

data.name: Warung Sika
data.address: Jl. Tanah Barak, Canggu, Badung, Bali
data.description: A Canggu warung with a nasi campur counter where you build your own plate of rice and local dishes.

data.name: Nasi Ayam Kedewatan Ibu Mangku
data.address: Jl. Raya Kedewatan, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali
data.description: A local favourite for nasi ayam, rice with shredded chicken, satay, egg and sambal, near Ubud's Kedewatan village.

data.name: Gunung Kawi
data.address: Jl. Bayu Brata, Tampaksiring, Gianyar, Bali
data.description: Ancient shrines carved into a cliff face in a river valley near Tampaksiring, reached by a long staircase through rice fields. Easy to add after Tirta Empul.

data.name: Yeh Pulu
data.address: Jl. Raya Semebaung, Bedulu, Blahbatuh, Gianyar, Bali
data.description: A rock-carved relief in a quiet rice-field setting near Goa Gajah, much less visited than its famous neighbour.

data.name: Pura Taman Ayun
data.description: A royal temple of the Mengwi dynasty with moats, lawns and tiered meru shrines, part of Bali's UNESCO-listed cultural landscape. Quiet compared with the coastal temples.

data.name: Neka Art Museum
data.address: Jl. Raya Sanggingan, Kedewatan, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali
data.description: A museum in Sanggingan with Balinese and Indonesian paintings in a series of pavilions. A calm, shaded way to spend an hour.

data.name: Sarong or scarf for temple visits
Sturdy sandals or trainers for rice terraces and temple steps
Passport and visa-on-arrival or e-VOA confirmation

title: Paris in 4 days: art, food and hidden corners
description: Four unhurried days in Paris that pair the big sights (Sainte-Chapelle, the Louvre, Montmartre, the Eiffel Tower) with neighbourhood bistros, covered passages and market lunches. Suits first-timers who like museums, long lunches and walking between them.

data.name: Sainte-Chapelle and Notre-Dame de Paris
data.description: Start with the 13th-century royal chapel, whose stained glass fills the upper level with colour (book a timed ticket), then walk to the restored Notre-Dame and its parvis.

data.name: Lunch at Marché des Enfants Rouges
data.description: Paris's oldest covered market has stalls serving Moroccan, Japanese, Lebanese and French lunches. Eat at the shared tables, then stroll up into the Marais.

data.name: Musée Picasso
data.description: A large collection of Picasso's paintings, sculpture and sketchbooks in a 17th-century mansion, shown roughly in the order he made them.

data.name: Dinner at Chez Janou
data.description: Lively Provençal bistro near the Place des Vosges, known for its long list of pastis and a shared bowl of chocolate mousse for dessert. Book ahead.

data.name: Musée du Louvre
data.description: Pick a few rooms rather than trying to see everything: the Mona Lisa, the Greek and Roman galleries and the Egyptian antiquities fill a good morning. Pre-book a time slot.

data.name: Lunch at Juvéniles
data.description: Long-running wine bar by the Palais-Royal with a short, changing menu of French bistro dishes and a good by-the-glass list.

data.name: Musée d'Orsay
data.description: Impressionist and post-Impressionist masterpieces inside a former railway station. Walk through the Tuileries gardens and across the Seine to get there.
data.address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris, France

data.name: Dinner at Allard
data.description: Classic Saint-Germain bistro cooking in an old-fashioned dining room; the French classics such as roast duck and frogs' legs are the reason to come.
data.address: 41 Rue Saint-André des Arts, 75006 Paris, France

data.name: Sacré-Cœur and Montmartre
data.description: Climb to the white basilica for views over the city, then wander the village lanes of the hill. Arriving early means fewer crowds on the steps.
data.address: 35 Rue du Chevalier de la Barre, 75018 Paris, France

data.name: Lunch at Le Coq & Fils
data.description: Antoine Westermann's poultry-focused bistro on Montmartre's Rue Lepic (formerly Le Coq Rico). The roast bird is the dish to order.

data.name: Galerie Vivienne and Passage des Panoramas
data.description: Two of the 19th-century covered passages: tiled floors, glass roofs, bookshops, tea rooms and small shops. Walk between them via the Grands Boulevards side.
data.address: 4 Rue des Petits Champs, 75002 Paris, France

data.name: Dinner at Bouillon Chartier
data.description: A bustling belle-époque dining hall serving simple French staples at friendly prices, with waiters in black and white. Expect a queue and share a table.
data.address: 7 Rue du Faubourg Montmartre, 75009 Paris, France

data.name: Musée Rodin
data.description: Rodin's sculptures, including The Thinker and The Gates of Hell, set in a mansion and a quiet rose garden. The garden alone is worth the visit.

data.name: Lunch at Le Petit Cler
data.description: Relaxed café-bistro on the market street of Rue Cler, with tartines, salads and French lunch plates. Pick up cheese or fruit from the street stalls afterwards.

data.name: Eiffel Tower and Champ de Mars
data.description: Go up the tower if you have pre-booked tickets, or simply picnic on the Champ de Mars lawns and view it from below. Cross the river to Trocadéro for the classic view.
data.address: Champ de Mars, 5 Avenue Anatole France, 75007 Paris, France

data.name: Seine river cruise
data.description: A one-hour boat trip from the foot of the Eiffel Tower, passing Notre-Dame, the Louvre and the Musée d'Orsay: a good way to see the city's bridges and monuments.
data.address: Port de la Bourdonnais, 75007 Paris, France

data.name: Hotel Jeanne d'Arc Le Marais
data.description: Small, well-reviewed three-star hotel on a quiet street in the Marais, close to the Place des Vosges and an easy walk to Notre-Dame, the Picasso Museum and the Bastille.

data.name: Le Comptoir du Relais
data.description: Yves Camdeborde's much-loved Saint-Germain bistro, recognised by the Michelin Guide. Book well ahead for dinner, or go for a weekend lunch.

data.name: Breizh Café (Marais)
data.address: 109 Rue Vieille du Temple, 75003 Paris, France
data.description: Buckwheat galettes and sweet crêpes with Breton cider, using good-quality ingredients. A tasty and relaxed Marais lunch.

data.name: L'Ami Jean
data.description: Stéphane Jégo's Basque-influenced bistro near the Eiffel Tower, known for generous, hearty cooking and its rice pudding dessert.

data.name: Septime
data.description: Michelin-starred modern French restaurant in the Bastille area. Tables are hard to get, so book as early as you can.

data.name: Bouillon Racine
data.description: Listed Art Nouveau brasserie from 1906 near the Sorbonne, with mosaic tiles and carved wood, serving traditional French dishes.

data.name: Musée de la Vie romantique
data.description: Small museum in a pretty 1830 house with a courtyard garden and tea room, devoted to the Romantic era and to George Sand.

data.name: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont
data.description: Hilly 19th-century park with a lake, cliffs, a suspension bridge and a hilltop temple. Locals come here for picnics and views.

data.name: Coulée verte René-Dumont (Promenade plantee)
data.address: Viaduc des Arts, Avenue Daumesnil, 75012 Paris, France
data.description: An elevated garden walkway on a former railway viaduct, starting near Bastille and running east above the rooftops, with craft studios beneath.

data.name: Rue Crémieux
data.description: Pedestrian street of pastel-painted houses near the Gare de Lyon, one of the prettiest and quietest little streets in Paris.

data.name: Light rain jacket or compact umbrella
Small day bag with a zip

title: Barcelona in 4 days: Gaudí, tapas and the sea
description: Four days in Barcelona that balance Gaudí's headline buildings with old-town tapas bars, vermouth in Gràcia and a slow afternoon at the beach. Suits first-time visitors who like walking, architecture and eating in small, busy bars.

data.name: Museu Picasso
data.description: Early works and the Las Meninas series in a row of medieval palaces on Carrer de Montcada. It shows how Picasso's years in Barcelona shaped him. Book a time slot in advance.

data.name: Lunch at Cal Pep
data.description: Counter-only tapas bar in El Born, famous for its seafood and market ingredients. There are no bookings, so arrive when it opens and be ready to queue.
data.address: Plaça de les Olles 8, 08003 Barcelona, Spain

data.name: Barcelona Cathedral and the Gothic Quarter
data.description: Visit the Gothic cathedral and its cloister (with its resident geese), then wander the lanes of the Barri Gòtic, past Roman remains and quiet squares.
data.address: Pla de la Seu s/n, 08002 Barcelona, Spain

data.name: Dinner at Can Culleretes
data.description: One of the city's oldest restaurants, in the Gothic Quarter, serving traditional Catalan dishes in old dining rooms. Try the Catalan classics such as canelons or a fish stew.

data.name: Sagrada Família
data.description: Gaudí's unfinished basilica, with a forest-like nave and glowing stained glass. Pre-book a timed ticket, and add a tower visit if you want the views.

data.name: Lunch at Cervecería Catalana
data.description: A buzzing Eixample tapas bar with a long counter and a huge menu of montaditos, grilled meats and seafood tapas. A reliable favourite with locals.

data.name: Casa Batlló
data.description: Gaudí's colourful house on the Passeig de Gràcia, with a skeletal facade and rippling interiors. The roof terrace and light well are the highlights.

data.name: Dinner at Bar Cañete
data.description: Lively tapas bar near the Liceu, known for market-fresh seafood and classic dishes served at a long counter. Booking is recommended.
data.address: Carrer de la Unió 17, 08001 Barcelona, Spain

data.name: Park Güell
data.description: Gaudí's hillside park, with the mosaic bench, the dragon staircase and views over the city to the sea. Entry to the monumental area needs a timed ticket.

data.name: Vermouth lunch at Bar Bodega Quimet
data.description: A small, old-style Gràcia bodega serving vermouth from the tap with anchovies, olives and tinned seafood. A classic Catalan way to start the afternoon.

data.name: Casa Vicens
data.description: Gaudí's first major house, covered in tiles and brick in a colourful, early style. It is a peaceful visit in the heart of Gràcia.
data.address: Carrer de les Carolines 20, 08012 Barcelona, Spain

data.name: Dinner at Taverna El Glop
data.description: Rustic, cosy Catalan tavern in Gràcia with paella-style rice dishes, grilled meats and seasonal specials such as calçots. Reserve ahead at busy times.
data.address: Carrer de Sant Lluís 24, 08012 Barcelona, Spain

data.name: Mercat de la Boqueria
data.description: Barcelona's most famous food market: stalls of fruit, jamon, cheese and seafood. Have a coffee and a small bite at a counter, and go early before the crowds.

data.name: Fundació Joan Miró
data.description: A bright modernist building holding a large collection of Miró's paintings, sculpture and tapestries, with a rooftop terrace and views across the city.
data.address: Parc de Montjuïc, Carrer de Joan de Garay s/n, 08038 Barcelona, Spain

data.name: Lunch at Quimet & Quimet
data.description: Tiny standing-room bar in Poble Sec, famous for creative montaditos made with tinned seafood and cheese. Don't expect a seat.
data.address: Carrer del Poeta Cabanyes 25, 08004 Barcelona, Spain

data.name: Barceloneta Beach
data.description: Finish the trip on the city beach: a swim in summer or a long walk along the promenade in cooler months, with a drink at a chiringuito.
data.address: Platja de la Barceloneta, 08003 Barcelona, Spain

data.name: Casa Camper Barcelona
data.description: Design-led boutique hotel on a pedestrian street in El Raval, minutes from La Rambla and the Boqueria. Rooms have a sleeping area and a separate lounge, and there is a roof terrace and 24-hour snack bar.

data.name: El Xampanyet
data.description: Standing-room cava and anchovy bar next to the Picasso Museum, in business for generations, with blue tiles and a marble counter.

data.name: La Cova Fumada
data.description: Unmarked Barceloneta bodega said to be the birthplace of the bomba, a potato-and-meat croquette. Queues form early and there are no bookings.

data.name: Els Quatre Gats
data.description: Modernista cafe where the young Picasso held his first exhibition. Come for the history and the setting as much as the food.

data.name: Can Solé
data.address: Carrer de Sant Carles 4, 08003 Barcelona, Spain
data.description: Seafood and rice restaurant in Barceloneta that has been serving fishermen and visitors since 1903. Order the arròs negre or the fish and seafood rice.

data.name: Bar del Pla
data.description: Modern Catalan tapas in El Born, with a short menu of seasonal dishes and a good wine list. A relaxed option for an early dinner.

data.name: Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau
data.address: Carrer de Sant Quintí 89, 08041 Barcelona, Spain
data.description: A former hospital complex of colourful Modernista pavilions and gardens by Domènech i Montaner, a short walk from the Sagrada Família and far quieter.

data.name: Parc del Laberint d'Horta
data.description: Barcelona's oldest garden: an 18th-century neoclassical park with a cypress hedge maze, ponds and a quiet, romantic feel.

data.name: Museu Frederic Marès
data.address: Plaça de Sant Iu 5, 08002 Barcelona, Spain
data.description: A quirky sculpture museum in the Gothic Quarter, with a leafy courtyard cafe tucked behind the cathedral.

data.name: Bunkers del Carmel
data.address: Carrer de Marià Labèrnia s/n, 08032 Barcelona, Spain
data.description: Former Civil War anti-aircraft battery on a hilltop with 360-degree views over the city and the sea. Locals bring picnics at sunset.

data.name: Swimwear and a light beach towel
Cross-body bag with a zip (pickpockets target crowded areas)
Light layer that covers shoulders for churches
Pre-booked tickets for Sagrada Família and Park Güell

title: Amsterdam in 3 days: canals, museums and brown cafes
description: Three easy days in Amsterdam that mix the big museums with canal-side wandering, Dutch comfort food and a windy-day park. Suits first-time visitors who want culture and good food without a rushed schedule, all reachable on foot or by tram.

data.name: Anne Frank House
data.description: Visit the canal-side house where Anne Frank's family hid. Tickets are sold online in advance only, so book as early as you can.

data.name: Lunch at Café de Reiger
data.description: Traditional brown cafe in the Jordaan with a restaurant in the back room. Order Dutch classics such as pea soup or hutspot, plus a slice of apple pie.

data.name: Rijksmuseum
data.description: Dutch Golden Age art, including Rembrandt's Night Watch, plus Delftware and ship models. Choose a few galleries rather than trying to cover everything.

data.name: Dinner at Moeders
data.description: Cosy Jordaan restaurant with walls covered in photos of mothers and a menu of Dutch home cooking such as stamppot and stews. Reserve a table.

data.name: Van Gogh Museum
data.description: The largest collection of Van Gogh's paintings and letters, shown in the order of his life. Book a time slot and go early.

data.name: Albert Cuyp Market and street-food lunch
data.description: A busy daily street market in De Pijp. Graze on a fresh stroopwafel, Dutch herring or cheese samples, and look at the stalls selling flowers and household goods.

data.name: Vondelpark
data.description: Amsterdam's best-known city park. Walk or cycle past ponds and lawns, and stop at one of the cafe terraces. A good, free break between museums.

data.name: Dinner at Foodhallen
data.description: Indoor food hall in a former tram depot with stalls serving Dutch bitterballen, Vietnamese, Mexican and more. Good for groups with different tastes.

data.name: Begijnhof and the Nine Streets
data.description: Step into the Begijnhof's quiet courtyard garden, then browse the small independent shops and cafes in the Nine Streets between the main canals.

data.name: Apple pie at Winkel 43
data.description: Corner cafe on the Noordermarkt, long known for its apple pie with whipped cream. Sit outside by the Noorderkerk if the weather is good.

data.name: Hortus Botanicus
data.description: One of the world's oldest botanical gardens, with a palm house, a butterfly house and a glasshouse of tropical plants, in a calm corner of the Plantage.

data.name: Dinner at De Kas
data.description: Restaurant in a restored greenhouse in Frankendael Park, serving a seasonal set menu built around vegetables grown on site. Book ahead.

data.name: Hotel Estheréa
data.description: Family-run canal-house hotel on the Singel, in the heart of the canal ring. Walk to Dam Square, the Nine Streets and the Jordaan, with a quiet lounge looking onto the water.

data.name: Café de Klos
data.description: Rowdy, meat-focused spot known for its ribs and chicken. A real local favourite late in the evening.

data.name: Hap-Hmm
data.description: Old-school Dutch dinner house near the Vondelpark with a short menu that changes daily. Large portions, simple prices, plenty of locals.

data.name: Bakers & Roasters
data.address: Eerste Jacob van Campenstraat 54H, Amsterdam, Netherlands
data.description: A popular brunch spot in De Pijp with a Kiwi-Brazilian menu. Good for a relaxed breakfast or lunch.

data.name: Brouwerij 't IJ
data.description: Craft brewery and taproom beneath the De Gooyer windmill in the east. Order a tasting of the house beers with some local cheese.

data.name: The Pancake Bakery
data.description: Canal-side restaurant in a historic warehouse that serves large Dutch pannenkoeken, sweet and savoury. Good for families.

data.name: Museum Het Schip
data.description: A striking brick housing block and former post office from the Amsterdam School of architecture, with a museum and a guided tour of the building.

data.name: Café 't Smalle
data.description: Tiny brown cafe with a terrace on a quiet Jordaan canal corner. A good place for a late afternoon drink away from the main streets.

data.name: Westergasfabriek
data.description: Former gasworks turned into a cultural park with cafes, a cinema and open lawns. Popular with locals at weekends, but off most tourist routes.

data.name: Jacob Hooy & Co
data.description: Traditional herb and spice shop, with wooden drawers and old apothecary jars, selling teas, remedies and sweets since the 18th century.

data.name: Comfortable shoes for cobbles and canal bridges
Warm layers for wind off the water
Pre-booked tickets for Anne Frank House, Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum

title: New York in 1 week: classic sights, great food and Brooklyn views
description: A week in New York City covering the headline sights, museums, neighbourhood walks and a strong lineup of classic eating, from pastrami and pizza to dumplings and steak. Suits first-time visitors who want a good balance of icons and local favourites.

data.name: Grand Central Terminal
data.description: A Beaux-Arts rail terminal with a star-painted ceiling, the Whispering Gallery and the famous four-faced clock on the main concourse.

data.name: Joe's Pizza (Broadway)
data.description: Classic New York slice joint in the Midtown mix. Folded cheese or pepperoni slices are the order; eat them on the go.

data.name: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)
data.description: Modern and contemporary art from Van Gogh and Picasso to Warhol. Pick two or three floors rather than trying to see everything.

data.name: Top of the Rock
data.description: Rockefeller Center's observation decks, with views of Central Park to the north and the Empire State Building to the south. Book a time slot in advance.

data.name: Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island ferry
data.description: Take the ferry from Battery Park to Liberty Island and Ellis Island, where millions of immigrants arrived. Book ahead and arrive early for security.
data.address: Castle Clinton, Battery Park, New York, NY 10004

data.name: 9/11 Memorial and Museum
data.description: Reflecting pools mark the footprints of the Twin Towers, with an underground museum documenting the attacks. A sombre visit; allow time.

data.name: Fraunces Tavern Museum and Stone Street
data.description: An 18th-century tavern and museum on American Revolution history, then a stroll down cobbled Stone Street and the narrow canyons of Wall Street.

data.name: Joe's Shanghai
data.description: Soup dumplings (xiao long bao) filled with pork or crab and pork. Bite a small hole first to release the steam and broth.

data.name: Tenement Museum
data.description: Guided tours of restored tenement apartments that tell the stories of the immigrant families who lived there. Book a tour in advance.

data.name: Katz's Delicatessen
data.description: Hand-carved pastrami on rye at the historic Lower East Side deli, open since 1888. Keep your ticket safe and tip the carver.
data.address: 205 E Houston St, New York, NY 10002

data.name: Washington Square Park and Greenwich Village
data.description: Walk through the arch and fountain, then wander the Village's brownstone streets, bookshops and cafes.
data.address: Washington Square Park, New York, NY 10012

data.name: Village Vanguard
data.description: A historic basement jazz club where many famous albums were recorded. Check the week's line-up and book ahead.

data.name: Whitney Museum of American Art
data.description: American art from the 20th century to today, with outdoor terraces overlooking the Hudson River and the start of the High Line.

data.name: Los Tacos No. 1 (Chelsea Market)
data.description: Tacos made with handmade tortillas, including adobada from the spit and carne asada, served in the busy Chelsea Market.

data.name: The High Line
data.description: Walk the elevated park built on a former freight rail line, with public art, gardens and Hudson River views, north to Hudson Yards.
data.address: Gansevoort St and Washington St, New York, NY 10014

data.name: Via Carota
data.description: Italian restaurant on a West Village corner known for seasonal vegetables and handmade pasta. Arrive early for a table.

data.name: Central Park: The Mall and Bethesda Terrace
data.description: Walk the tree-lined Mall to Bethesda Terrace and fountain, then on to the lake and Bow Bridge.
data.address: Bethesda Terrace, Central Park, New York, NY 10024

data.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
data.description: One of the world's largest art museums, from Egyptian temples to European paintings. Choose a few galleries rather than trying to cover it all.

data.name: Apollo Theater
data.description: The historic Harlem theatre that launched many careers, famous for its Amateur Night. Take a tour or see a show.

data.name: Red Rooster Harlem
data.description: Marcus Samuelsson's Harlem restaurant, serving soul-food-inspired American cooking, with fried chicken among the favourites.

data.name: Walk the Brooklyn Bridge to DUMBO
data.description: Walk the pedestrian promenade from Manhattan over the East River, with skyline views, to the cobbled streets of DUMBO. Keep to the pedestrian side.
data.address: Brooklyn Bridge Pedestrian Walkway, Park Row, New York, NY 10038

data.name: Juliana's Pizza
data.description: Coal-oven pizza in DUMBO, with thin crusts and a simple topping list. Good to share.

data.name: Domino Park
data.description: A Williamsburg waterfront park on the site of the old Domino Sugar refinery, with skyline views and preserved industrial machinery.

data.name: Peter Luger Steak House
data.description: A Williamsburg steakhouse dating from 1887, known for its porterhouse for two. Reserve ahead.

data.name: American Museum of Natural History
data.description: Dinosaur skeletons, the blue whale model and the Hayden Planetarium, across the street from Central Park.
data.address: 200 Central Park W, New York, NY 10024

data.name: Barney Greengrass
data.description: A century-old Upper West Side appetising shop and restaurant, known for smoked fish and scrambled eggs with lox.

data.name: SoHo shopping: Prince Street and Broadway
data.description: Browse SoHo's cast-iron streets and boutiques around Prince Street and Broadway for fashion, design and gifts.
data.address: Prince St and Broadway, New York, NY 10012

data.name: Balthazar
data.description: A classic SoHo brasserie with steak frites, shellfish towers and a lively dining room. A fitting last dinner.

data.name: Washington Square Hotel
data.description: A well-reviewed, historic hotel in Greenwich Village, just off Washington Square Park. A walkable base with good subway access to Midtown, Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn.

data.name: Russ & Daughters Cafe
data.description: Smoked salmon, bagels and babka at a Lower East Side institution. The sit-down cafe is good for breakfast or brunch.

data.name: Nom Wah Tea Parlor
data.description: A long-running Chinatown dim sum restaurant on Doyers Street, serving classics such as dumplings and rice rolls.

data.name: Lucali
data.description: Brick-oven pizza and calzone in Carroll Gardens, with a short menu and a candlelit dining room.

data.name: Gramercy Tavern
data.description: A Danny Meyer restaurant serving seasonal American cooking in a warm dining room, with a more casual tavern at the front.

data.name: The Cloisters
data.address: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040
data.description: The Met's medieval art museum, built from European monastery fragments in Fort Tryon Park, with herb gardens and Hudson River views.

data.name: Green-Wood Cemetery
data.description: A hilly 19th-century cemetery in Brooklyn with Victorian monuments, quiet paths and distant views of the Statue of Liberty and Manhattan.

data.name: The Morgan Library & Museum
data.description: J. P. Morgan's private library and its rare manuscripts, with exhibitions and a glass-roofed courtyard. Often overlooked in Midtown.

data.name: Arthur Avenue Retail Market
data.description: The heart of the Bronx's Little Italy: an indoor market with delis, bakeries and pasta shops, surrounded by Italian-American restaurants.

data.name: Layers and a compact umbrella or rain jacket
Passport and ESTA or visa confirmation
Some cash for restaurants that do not take cards
Small day bag for museums and walks

title: Lisbon in 4 days: hills, tiles, fado and a day in Sintra
description: Four days in Lisbon with time for Alfama's lanes and fado, the monuments of Belém, a fairytale day trip to Sintra and a slow last day in Chiado. Suits curious walkers who like seafood, custard tarts and a few steep hills.

data.name: Castelo de São Jorge
data.description: Walk the walls of the hilltop castle for views over the red rooftops and the Tagus. Go up by foot or tram through Alfama's steep lanes.
data.address: Rua de Santa Cruz do Castelo, Lisbon, Portugal

data.name: Lunch at Chapitô à Mesa
data.description: Restaurant in the Chapitô arts centre just below the castle, with a terrace looking across the rooftops to the river and a menu of modern Portuguese dishes.

data.name: Museu do Fado
data.description: A small museum on the history of fado, with recordings, instruments and the story of its great singers. It is a good primer before an evening of live fado.
data.address: Largo do Chafariz de Dentro 1, Lisbon, Portugal

data.name: Dinner and fado at Clube de Fado
data.description: Dinner-and-fado venue beside the cathedral, with live fado singers and Portuguese dishes. Reserve ahead.
data.address: Rua de São João da Praça 94, Lisbon, Portugal

data.name: Jerónimos Monastery
data.description: Manueline masterpiece from the Age of Discoveries, with an ornate carved cloister. Go early, before the tour groups arrive.

data.name: Pastéis de Belém
data.description: The bakery that made the custard tart famous, using a recipe from 1837. Eat a warm tart with cinnamon and a coffee.

data.name: Torre de Belém
data.description: The 16th-century riverside tower is a symbol of the Age of Discoveries. Walk along the waterfront and photograph it from outside, or climb it if the queue is short.

data.name: Lunch at Time Out Market Lisboa
data.description: A large food hall in the old Ribeira market, with stalls from some of Lisbon's best-known chefs and producers. Pick several small plates and share.

data.name: Pena Palace
data.description: The colourful hilltop palace above Sintra, with terraces and views to the Atlantic. Take an early train from Rossio and book tickets in advance.

data.name: Lunch at Tascantiga
data.description: A small, casual restaurant in Sintra's old centre serving petiscos, or Portuguese small plates. Arrive early or be prepared to queue.
data.address: Escadinhas da Fonte da Pipa 2-4, Sintra, Portugal

data.name: Quinta da Regaleira
data.description: A romantic estate with a neo-Manueline palace, tunnels and the spiral Initiation Well. Wear shoes with good grip, as the paths can be slippery.
data.address: Rua Barbosa du Bocage, Sintra, Portugal

data.name: Dinner at Cervejaria Ramiro
data.description: Lisbon's famous seafood restaurant. Order shellfish by weight, followed by the prego steak sandwich. There are no bookings, so expect a wait.

data.name: Convento do Carmo
data.description: The roofless Gothic ruins of a convent church wrecked in the 1755 earthquake, with an archaeological museum. Take the Santa Justa Lift or the walk up to reach it.

data.name: Lunch at Taberna da Rua das Flores
data.description: Small tasca with a handwritten, daily-changing menu of Portuguese petiscos and traditional dishes. It is popular, so arrive early or book.

data.name: LX Factory
data.description: A former industrial complex under the 25 de Abril bridge, now full of independent shops, a famous bookshop, cafes and street art.
data.address: Rua Rodrigues de Faria 103, Lisbon, Portugal

data.name: Sunset at Miradouro de Santa Catarina
data.description: A popular terrace viewpoint over the river and the 25 de Abril bridge. Locals bring a drink to watch the sun go down.
data.address: Rua de Santa Catarina, Lisbon, Portugal

data.name: Memmo Alfama
data.description: Boutique hotel in a restored 19th-century building in Alfama, a short walk from the castle and the cathedral. Terrace with views over the river, a pool and a wine bar.

data.name: Prado
data.address: Travessa das Pedras Negras 2, Lisbon, Portugal
data.description: Farm-to-table restaurant in Alfama led by chef António Galapito, working with small-scale producers and organic wines. Michelin-listed.

data.name: Cantinho do Avillez
data.address: Rua dos Duques de Bragança 7, Lisbon, Portugal
data.description: Chef José Avillez's casual Chiado restaurant, offering modern takes on Portuguese dishes in a lively room.

data.name: Tasca da Esquina
data.description: Chef Vítor Sobral's modern tasca in Campo de Ourique, serving traditional Portuguese flavours in small dishes. Reservations are advised.

data.name: Manteigaria
data.description: Specialist pastel de nata bakery in Chiado where you can watch the tarts come out of the oven. A good stop before or after Chiado's shops.

data.name: Casa Piriquita
data.description: The Sintra bakery known for travesseiros, pillow-shaped almond pastries, and queijadas. A good snack stop if you add a second day in Sintra.

data.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
data.address: Rua da Madre de Deus 4, Lisbon, Portugal
data.description: Portugal's national tile museum, in a former convent with a gilded baroque church, with centuries of azulejos and a long panel of Lisbon before the earthquake.

data.name: Palácio Fronteira
data.address: Largo de São Domingos de Benfica 1, Lisbon, Portugal
data.description: A 17th-century palace on the edge of the city with formal gardens and walls covered in blue-and-white azulejos. The interior is visited by guided tour.

data.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
data.description: One of the highest viewpoints in the city, with a sweeping panorama of the castle, the river and the centre. Less crowded than Alfama's terraces.

data.name: Jardim Botânico de Lisboa
data.address: Rua da Escola Politécnica 58, Lisbon, Portugal
data.description: A peaceful 19th-century botanical garden in Príncipe Real, with palms and shaded paths, and tropical plants a short walk from busy Bairro Alto.

data.name: Comfortable shoes with good grip for steep, polished cobbles

title: Rome in 5 days: ancient wonders, Roman food and hidden corners
description: Five unhurried days in the Eternal City: the Colosseum and Forum, the Vatican, the piazzas of the historic centre and Galleria Borghese, with Trastevere and Testaccio meals along the way. Suits first-time visitors who want the big sights, honest Roman cooking and room to wander.

data.name: Colosseum
data.description: Start at the great amphitheatre while the morning is cooler. Book a timed ticket in advance to skip the longest queues and look out over the arena floor.
data.address: Piazza del Colosseo, 1, 00184 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Roman Forum and Palatine Hill
data.description: Walk the Via Sacra through the civic heart of ancient Rome, then climb the Palatine for views back over the Forum. Check whether your Colosseum ticket includes entry.
data.address: Via della Salara Vecchia, 5/6, 00186 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Lunch at Ai Tre Scalini
data.description: Lively Monti wine bar for cured meats, cheeses and simple Roman plates, a short walk uphill from the Forum.

data.name: Dinner at Trattoria Monti
data.description: Small family-run trattoria cooking the food of the Marche region. Try the fried olives ascolane and the artichoke tortino, and book ahead.
data.address: Via di San Vito, 13a, 00185 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel
data.description: Book the earliest entry slot you can. Allow time for the Raphael Rooms and finish in Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel. Dress code: shoulders and knees covered.

data.name: Lunch at Pizzarium
data.description: Gabriele Bonci's celebrated pizza al taglio shop: choose a few seasonal slices and eat them at the outdoor tables. Expect a queue.
data.address: Via della Meloria, 43, 00136 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: St Peter's Basilica
data.description: Cross the colonnaded square to see Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's baldachin. If you have energy left, climb the dome for views over the city.
data.address: Piazza San Pietro, 00120 Città del Vaticano

data.name: Dinner at Da Enzo al 29
data.description: Much-loved Trastevere trattoria for carbonara, meatballs and braised artichokes. Arrive early or book, as the few tables fill fast.
data.address: Via dei Vascellari, 29, 00153 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Pantheon
data.description: Step inside the best-preserved building of ancient Rome and look up at the oculus in its famous dome. Visit early, before the tour groups arrive.
data.address: Piazza della Rotonda, 00186 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Capitoline Museums
data.description: Michelangelo's hilltop piazza leads to some of the world's oldest public museums, with the Capitoline Wolf, ancient statuary and a terrace over the Forum.
data.address: Piazza del Campidoglio, 1, 00186 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Lunch at Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina
data.description: Deli, wine cellar and restaurant in one. Order the carbonara and a board of cured meats and cheeses, and reserve ahead.
data.address: Via dei Giubbonari, 21, 00186 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Dinner at Armando al Pantheon
data.description: Family-run trattoria steps from the Pantheon, serving classic Roman cooking including pasta and offal dishes. Book well ahead.
data.address: Salita de' Crescenzi, 31, 00186 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Galleria Borghese
data.description: Bernini's sculptures and Caravaggio's paintings in a villa at the edge of Villa Borghese park. Entry is by timed reservation, so book well in advance.
data.address: Piazzale Scipione Borghese, 5, 00197 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Spanish Steps and Trevi Fountain
data.description: Stroll through Villa Borghese's Pincio terrace and down the Spanish Steps to the Trevi Fountain. Go at midday or later; it is quieter in the early morning.
data.address: Piazza di Trevi, 00187 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Aventine Keyhole and Orange Garden
data.description: Peek through the keyhole of the Knights of Malta gate for a perfectly framed view of St Peter's dome, then walk to the Orange Garden terrace over the Tiber.
data.address: Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta, 00153 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Dinner at Flavio al Velavevodetto
data.description: Testaccio trattoria built into the side of Monte Testaccio, a hill of ancient pottery fragments. Order the cacio e pepe, amatriciana or carbonara.
data.address: Via di Monte Testaccio, 97, 00153 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Basilica of Santa Maria in Trastevere
data.description: One of Rome's oldest churches, with glittering medieval gold mosaics. Afterwards, take a coffee on the fountain-centred piazza outside.
data.address: Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere, 00153 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Janiculum Hill viewpoint
data.description: Walk up through the lanes of Trastevere to the Janiculum terrace for a sweeping panorama over the domes and rooftops of Rome.
data.address: Piazzale Giuseppe Garibaldi, 00152 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Lunch at L'Osteria della Trippa
data.description: Michelin-listed neighbourhood trattoria in Trastevere. Tripe is the house speciality, with plenty of Roman pasta dishes for the less adventurous.
data.address: Via Goffredo Mameli, 15, 00153 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
data.description: Emperor Hadrian's mausoleum turned papal fortress. Climb to the rooftop terrace for views to St Peter's, then cross the Ponte Sant'Angelo as the light softens.

data.name: Boutique Hotel Campo de' Fiori
data.description: Small boutique hotel a minute from Campo de' Fiori, with a rooftop terrace overlooking the historic centre. A central base within walking distance of the Pantheon, Piazza Navona and Trastevere.
data.address: Via del Biscione, 6, 00186 Roma RM, Italy

data.name: Felice a Testaccio
data.address: Via Mastro Giorgio, 29, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
data.description: Testaccio institution famous for cacio e pepe finished at the table. Book well ahead.

data.name: Pizzeria Da Remo
data.address: Piazza di Santa Maria Liberatrice, 44, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
data.description: No-frills Testaccio pizzeria serving thin, crisp Roman pizza and fried rice supplì. Expect a queue.

data.name: Trattoria Pennestri
data.address: Via Giovanni da Empoli, 5, 00154 Roma RM, Italy
data.description: Michelin-listed Ostiense trattoria with market-fresh daily specials alongside traditional Roman first courses. Reserve in advance.

data.name: Santo Palato
data.description: Jewish-Roman and central Italian cooking near San Giovanni, with offal dishes and a large wine cellar.

data.name: Hosteria Grappolo d'Oro
data.address: Piazza della Cancelleria, 80, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
data.description: Veteran restaurant behind Piazza Navona serving hearty seasonal Roman cuisine, including tonnarelli cacio e pepe and Roman-style lamb.

data.name: Basilica di San Clemente
data.description: A medieval church built on an earlier basilica, which sits on ancient Roman buildings. Walk down through the layers of the excavations.

data.name: Quartiere Coppedè
data.description: A small fairy-tale district of eclectic early 20th-century villas designed by Gino Coppedè, centred on the Fountain of the Frogs.

data.name: Centrale Montemartini
data.description: A former power station where classical Roman sculpture stands among the turbines and boilers. Part of the Capitoline Museums.

data.name: Garbatella
data.address: Piazza Benedetto Brin, 00145 Roma RM, Italy
data.description: A 1920s garden suburb of courtyards, stairways and murals that locals still treat as a village within Rome.

data.name: Scarf or light layer to cover shoulders in churches
Power adapter for Italy (types F and L)
Refillable water bottle for the street fountains
Anti-theft day bag with a zip

title: Budapest in 3 days: thermal baths, Danube views and Hungarian food
description: Three days on both banks of the Danube: Parliament, Castle Hill and a long soak in a thermal bath, with Hungarian classics and ruin-bar culture in between. Suits first-time visitors and food-focused weekenders who want a paced route rather than a checklist.

data.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
data.description: Tour the neo-Gothic Parliament on the Danube bank and see the Holy Crown of Hungary. Guided visits have limited places, so book ahead.

data.name: Lunch at the Great Market Hall
data.description: Browse paprika, salami and pickles on the ground floor, then eat a Hungarian lunch or a lángos at the stalls upstairs.

data.name: Dohány Street Synagogue
data.description: One of the largest synagogues in the world, with the Jewish Museum and the Heroes' Garden next door. Check visiting arrangements before you go.

data.name: Dinner at Menza
data.description: Retro-chic restaurant on Liszt Ferenc tér serving modern Hungarian dishes such as lecsó and honey-mustard roast mangalica pork. Book a table.

data.name: Matthias Church and Fisherman's Bastion
data.description: Start on Castle Hill at the Gothic Matthias Church with its patterned tiled roof, then walk the turrets of the Fisherman's Bastion for views over the Danube and Parliament.

data.name: Lunch at Déryné Bistro
data.description: Long-running bistro at the foot of Castle Hill with a French-leaning menu, good for a relaxed lunch.

data.name: Citadella and Gellért Hill
data.description: Climb Gellért Hill to the Liberty Statue and the Citadella ramparts for the widest views of the Danube, its bridges and both halves of the city.

data.name: Dinner at Borkonyha
data.description: Inventive modern Hungarian cooking and a serious wine list in Lipótváros. Reserve well in advance.

data.name: St Stephen's Basilica
data.description: Budapest's great neoclassical basilica. Climb to the panorama terrace for a 360-degree view over the rooftops of Pest.

data.name: Lunch at Café Kör
data.description: Bustling all-day bistro a minute from the Basilica, with seasonal Hungarian cooking such as baked leg of lamb. Reserve for lunch if you can.

data.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
data.description: Soak in the vast neo-baroque thermal bath complex in City Park. Bring swimwear and flip-flops, and check the bath's website for any areas closed for renovation. Heroes' Square is nearby.

data.name: Dinner at Gundel
data.description: Historic restaurant beside City Park and the Zoo, serving classic Hungarian cooking including Gundel pancakes and Újházi chicken soup.

data.name: Hotel Moments Budapest
data.description: Contemporary hotel in a restored 19th-century palace on Andrássy Avenue, a few minutes from St Stephen's Basilica and the State Opera House. A handy base for Pest, with the metro on the doorstep.

data.name: Rosenstein
data.description: Jewish and Hungarian restaurant in Józsefváros known for pan-fried goose liver in Tokaji sauce, stuffed cabbage and cholent.

data.name: Kőleves Vendéglő
data.description: Jewish-Hungarian cooking in the ruin-bar quarter. Try the coconut-milk soup with prawns or the goose leg with red cabbage.

data.name: Két Szerecsen
data.description: Theatre-district bistro with Hungarian and international dishes such as beef cheek and mangalica pork shoulder.

data.name: Mazel Tov
data.description: Israeli-Mediterranean restaurant in the ruin-bar district, serving shakshuka, falafel and shawarma.

data.name: Costes Downtown
data.description: French-Hungarian tasting menus of four or six courses in Ferencváros, a refined alternative to the classics.

data.name: Memento Park
data.address: Balatoni út, Szabadkai utca sarok, 1223 Budapest, Hungary
data.description: An open-air museum on the city's southern edge where communist-era statues removed from Budapest's streets after 1989 are displayed.

data.name: Hospital in the Rock Nuclear Bunker Museum
data.description: A secret hospital and nuclear shelter inside Castle Hill's caves, now a museum of Budapest's wartime history. Visits are by guided tour.

data.name: Metropolitan Ervin Szabó Library
data.description: A working public library in the neo-baroque Wenckheim Palace, where visitors can see the ornate reading rooms. Ask at the desk about visiting.

data.name: Fiumei Road National Graveyard
data.description: Hungary's national pantheon, a leafy cemetery of ornate mausoleums where many of the country's leading figures are buried. Free to enter.

data.name: Swimsuit and flip-flops for the thermal baths
Comfortable walking shoes for hills and cobbles
Power adapter for Hungary (types C and F)
Small amount of Hungarian forint for market stalls

title: Prague in 3 days: castle views, Czech beer halls and quiet gardens
