description: Three days in Prague: the castle and Charles Bridge, the Old Town and Jewish Quarter, then Vyšehrad and Petřín, with Czech beer halls, historic cafés and quiet gardens along the way. Suits first-time visitors who like to walk and linger over lunch.

data.name: Prague Castle
data.description: See St Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, St George's Basilica and Golden Lane. Arrive early and buy a circuit ticket online to avoid the longest queues.

data.name: Lunch at Café Savoy
data.description: Neo-Renaissance café with a painted ceiling on the Malá Strana riverbank, serving Czech classics and pastries from its own bakery.

data.name: Kampa Island and Charles Bridge
data.description: Wander through Kampa Park and past the Lennon Wall, then cross Charles Bridge towards the Old Town as the afternoon light softens.

data.name: Dinner at U Modré kachničky
data.description: Candlelit Malá Strana restaurant known for roast duck and game in classic Czech cooking. Reserve ahead.

data.name: Old Town Square and Astronomical Clock
data.description: Watch the Astronomical Clock chime on the hour, climb the Old Town Hall tower for views, then see the Týn Church and the Jan Hus memorial.

data.name: Jewish Quarter and Old Jewish Cemetery
data.description: Visit the synagogues and the crowded Old Jewish Cemetery in Josefov. Check the Jewish Museum's ticketing and entry arrangements before you go.

data.name: Lunch at Lokál Dlouhááá
data.description: A modern take on the Czech beer hall, with tank Pilsner Urquell alongside svíčková, guláš and other classics. Reserve if you can.

data.name: Dinner at Pivovarský dům
data.description: Microbrewery in New Town with house beers and Czech mains. Try the beer tasting paddle with a classic like svíčková.

data.name: Vyšehrad
data.description: Stroll the ramparts of this riverside hilltop fort for views over the Vltava, then visit the Basilica of St Peter and St Paul and the cemetery where Dvořák and Smetana are buried.

data.name: Dancing House
data.description: Admire Vlado Milunić and Frank Gehry's playful 'Fred and Ginger' building from the embankment on your way back towards the centre.

data.name: Lunch at Café Louvre
data.description: Grand, high-ceilinged café on Národní, open since 1902. Come for a Czech lunch, coffee and apple strudel.

data.name: Petřín Hill and Lookout Tower
data.description: Ride the funicular or walk up through the orchards of Petřín to the lookout tower inspired by the Eiffel Tower, for a last panorama over the city.

data.name: Augustine, a Luxury Collection Hotel
data.description: Hotel in a restored 13th-century Augustinian monastery in Malá Strana, with its own brewery bar. A short walk from both the Castle and Charles Bridge.

data.name: Kantýna
data.description: Butcher-style canteen near Wenceslas Square where meat is cooked to order. Beef tartare and chalkboard steaks are the draw.

data.name: Terasa U Zlaté studně
data.description: Rooftop terrace restaurant below Prague Castle with a seasonal tasting menu and sunset views over the city.

data.name: Eska
data.description: Bakery, café and restaurant in a converted Karlín factory, with a Michelin Bib Gourmand for its modern Czech cooking.

data.name: Field
data.description: Tasting-menu restaurant in the Old Town built around seasonal Czech produce, with a Michelin star in recent years. Book well ahead.

data.name: Naše Maso
data.description: Butcher shop with a small bistro in the Dlouhá arcade, known for steak tartare, burgers and warm sausages.

data.name: Vrtba Garden
data.description: A terraced Baroque garden tucked behind a Malá Strana palace, with statues, sculpted hedges and views over the red rooftops.

data.name: Wallenstein Garden
data.description: A free Baroque garden beside the Senate with a grotto wall, an aviary and resident peacocks.

data.name: Letná Beer Garden
data.description: A favourite with locals: a relaxed beer garden in Letná Park with views over the Vltava and the Old Town rooftops.

data.name: Žižkov Television Tower
data.description: A 1980s TV tower with an observation deck and David Černý's crawling baby sculptures climbing its legs.

data.name: Comfortable shoes for cobblestones and hills
Power adapter for Czechia (types C and E)
Small amount of Czech koruna for cafés and tips
Day bag with a zip for crowded bridges and trams
